newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Albania parties seal agreement on election - OSCE.
newsitem.headline: Albania parties seal agreement on election - OSCE.

text.p: European envoy Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday Albanian politicians had agreed to go ahead with a general election on June 29, ending days of deadlock threatening to plunge the Balkan state into further crisis.

Vranitzky, mediating in Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) since widespread violence erupted in March, gave a pledge that the international community would now do everything possible to help the country to prepare the poll and post-election reconstruction.

"(Albanian) Prime Minister (Bashkim) Fino contacted me last night and he told me the political parties had agreed to solve the political situation in Albania...They have confirmed the election will be held on June 29," Vranitzky told a news conference," Vranitzky told a news conference.

Speaking after addressing the OSCE's Vienna-based permanent council, the former Austrian chancellor said a number of sticking points had been resolved, including the makeup of a central electoral commission and regional commissions.

He said President Sali Berisha, whose rightist Democratic Party won a huge majority in a disputed election a year ago, had conceded his power to nominate the heads of the commissions to Fino, a member of the main opposition Socialist Party.

Fino became prime minister in March when all political parties agreed to set up a national unity government aimed at halting further anarchy spreading across the former Stalinist state. Violence and looting broke out after weeks of protest by impoverished Albanians who lost their savings in pyramid investment schemes.

Vranitzky said all parties would have access to the media. Opposition parties last year complained that state-controlled television and radio were controlled by the Democrats and that they did not receive the same air time.
Vranitzky said the 54-nation OSCE would give its total support to help in preparing the election and would send as many observers as was deemed necessary in cooperation with the Council of Europe.
"We will help Albania. The whole international community is speaking with unanimity. There are no dissenting voices," he added.
